newsitem.title: UK: First Leisure sees good medium-term growth.
newsitem.headline: First Leisure sees good medium-term growth.

text.p: First Leisure Corporation expects to reap the benefits of a 100 million stg investment programme over the next three years or so, chief executive John Conlan said on Thursday.
He said First Leisure would invest it over the next two years with 55 million stg of investment planned for the current financial year.

"We will open 20 new businesses in the course of the year," Conlan told Reuters in a telephone interview. He said the real impact of the expansion on pre-tax profit would start to come through from 1998.
"We see the fruits of our strategy coming through over the next three years," said Conlan.
First Leisure plans to boost its nightclub capacity by 35 percent over the next 18 months, strengthening its hand in its biggest business where it is a market leader.
Turning to health and fitness, Conlan said six new clubs were planned for 1997 and a couple more for early next year.

"We are beginning to get some real momentum in this division," he said. But he noted that fitness club investments take longer to mature than nightclubs, the real benefits typically feeding through in the third year of operation.
First Leisure reported difficult trading conditions in bingo, a result of competition from the National Lottery

Total sales grew by 62 percent to 25.1 million stg, including new openings, but were down 17 percent on a like-for-like basis. Profits, affected by the policy of writing off launch costs in the first year of trading, fell 1.7 million stg to just 200,000 stg.
Conlan said that he hoped legislation would be approved fairly quickly to lift restrictions on bingo advertising and "restore a level playing field" with the lottery.

"That will enable the industry to get back the volume lost over the last 18 months or so," Conlan said, saying that bingo was a billion pound business which had been reliable for generations and could still thrive.
"We're going to stick with it," he said, nothing that bingo was only a small part of the group's activity.
